title: Acute Severe Asthma / Bronchospasm Exacerbation
guidelines: BTS/SIGN British Guideline on the Management of Asthma 2019
GINA Global Strategy for Asthma Management 2023
pathophysiology: Acute inflammatory bronchoconstriction, airway mucosal edema, and mucus plugging causing severe expiratory airflow limitation.

facts.onset: My chest started getting tight last night and my blue inhaler stopped giving me relief two hours ago.
facts.symptoms: I can only speak two or three words at a time. I am wheezing and my chest feels like it is clamped shut.
facts.history: I have had asthma since childhood. I take a salbutamol reliever and a beclometasone inhaler, but I ran out of preventer last month. No drug allergies.
facts.risk: I was hospitalized two years ago for a severe asthma attack in the intensive care unit.
facts.exam: Patient is sitting upright in tripod position, speaking in monosyllables. Accessory muscle use visible. Extensive bilateral expiratory polyphonic wheeze. Heart rate 116 bpm, respiratory rate 30/min.

peak-flow.name: Bedside Peak Expiratory Flow (PEF)
peak-flow.result: Peak flow 180 L/min (predicted 520 L/min, ~35% of predicted/personal best).
peak-flow.interpretation: Severe airflow limitation (< 50% predicted); fulfills criteria for acute severe asthma.
peak-flow.why: Immediate objective quantification of airflow obstruction severity.

blood-gas.name: Arterial Blood Gas (ABG)
blood-gas.result: pH 7.43, PaCO2 32 mmHg, HCO3 21 mmol/L, PaO2 62 mmHg (on room air).
blood-gas.interpretation: Type 1 respiratory failure with acute respiratory alkalosis secondary to tachypnea; any rise in PaCO2 signifies impending respiratory muscle exhaustion.
blood-gas.why: Assess ventilation, oxygenation, and monitor for hypercapnic exhaustion in acute severe asthma.

chest-xray.name: Portable Chest X-ray
chest-xray.result: Hyperinflated lung fields; no pneumothorax, consolidation, or pneumomediastinum detected.
chest-xray.interpretation: Consistent with air-trapping in asthma; excludes secondary pneumothorax complication.
chest-xray.why: Check for complications (e.g., pneumothorax) if presentation is severe or deteriorating.

ct-chest.name: CT Chest
ct-chest.result: Not performed; high radiation risk without acute indication.
ct-chest.interpretation: Not indicated in initial management of acute asthma exacerbation.
ct-chest.why: Acute bedside bronchodilation and oxygenation take precedence; CT is contraindicated without suspecting specific structural complications.

expected_actions: High-flow oxygen titrated to target SpO2 93-95%
Nebulized high-dose beta-2 agonist (Salbutamol 5mg) driven by oxygen
Add nebulized Ipratropium bromide (0.5mg) for severe features
Early systemic corticosteroids (Oral Prednisolone 40-50mg or IV Hydrocortisone 100mg)
Urgent escalation to Senior Physician or ICU if no rapid improvement
critical_errors: Administering sedative or anxiolytic drugs during an acute asthma exacerbation (causes fatal respiratory depression)
Delaying systemic corticosteroid administration beyond 1 hour of presentation
Failing to recognize life-threatening signs (normalizing or rising PaCO2, silent chest, exhaustion)
